title: Premature Module Segmentation (Shotgun Surgery Modules)
pattern: Splitting a highly cohesive, tightly coupled set of types (like a struct, its main enum status, and its simple validation function) into multiple distinct files/modules.
why_bad: Forces developers to perform "shotgun surgery" across multiple files to make a simple, unified change (e.g., adding a status variant requires modifying `status.rs`, updating validation logic in `validation.rs`, and adjusting the struct in `order.rs`). This ruins the benefits of modular design and increases cognitive load.
detection: Identify tiny, single-type modules (less than 30 lines) where any modification requires simultaneous edits to adjacent files within the same directory.
counterexample: Very large frameworks where file split is necessary to avoid hitting compiler output limits or to manage thousands of lines of highly complex code.
source: *Eric Evans - Domain-Driven Design (2003)*, Chapter 5, "Modules" (High cohesion / Low coupling, p. 109); *Martin Fowler - Refactoring (1999)*, Chapter 3, "Shotgun Surgery".
